title: RAW_UNSCREENED: Observation versus rejected explanation in a natural-history entry
summary: Pliny's vine passage preserves a concrete report, an attributed contrary belief, and an experience-based correction while also enumerating five support classes. A target reading could therefore encode evidential commitment and correction, rather than treating every adjacent noun as a stable object list.

design.mechanism: A source report distinguishes an observed feature from a prior explanation that experience rejects; a later finite classification records the corrected alternatives. The semantic change is commitment status and replacement, not form repetition.
design.source_example: Pliny reports the belief that box slips from an untrimmed tree would survive, then says experience has ended that notion; in the same chapter he enumerates five vine support arrangements. The passage thus contains report, rejected explanation and corrected classification.
design.target_endpoint: The already admitted complete f17r.5 Herbal record in GDT768, where `cthy chor shor` are consecutive part-like cells followed by later fields, and the complete f29v.1 local record in GDT625.
design.reading_a: A report/correction register: one clause records an observation, another marks an inherited or attributed explanation as rejected, and a later field states the corrected class or consequence.
design.reading_b: A neutral inventory/classification: all neighbouring cells are assertions of equal status; apparent contrast is merely a list of parts, variants or states.
design.observable_difference: Reading A predicts a stable commitment transition: an attributed/uncertain claim is followed by a correction marker and a replacement consequence, with the same subject carried across the transition. Reading B predicts no change in commitment status and permits equivalent co-listing. The distinction requires a written correction or attribution cue; a rare word or line position cannot supply it.
design.smallest_test: Across already admitted complete Herbal entries, freeze any independently observable attribution/correction cue and test one held replacement consequence. If no such cue exists, retain both readings without assigning an evidential meaning.
design.nearest_rival: A flat nominal inventory or feature taxonomy, including the Pliny XV variant model above.
assumption_costs: The source's epistemic convention may not belong to the target register.
Attribution and correction cues need independent visual or textual evidence.
No prior working gloss may be used as a correction marker.
design.strongest_likely_failure: The admitted target lines contain no independently bound claim, attribution or correction fields; the proposal would then be a source precedent without a target consequence.
